title: Understanding One-hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding is a way to represent categorical data as binary vectors. Each category is represented by a vector with a single high (1) bit and all other bits low (0).

title: How Many Codons?
text: Each DNA string is made up of 3,000 letters. Since a codon consists of $$3$$ letters, how many codons are there in a single DNA string?

title: Calculate Number of Codons
text: Calculate the number of codons in a DNA string with 3,000 letters.

title: Possible Codons
text: There are $$4$$ possible letters (T, G, C, A) and each codon is made up of $$3$$ letters. How many possible codons can be formed?

title: Calculate Possible Codons
text: Calculate the number of possible codons using the formula for permutations with repetition: $$4^3$$.

title: One-hot Encoding Dimensions
text: To find the number of dimensions for one-hot encoding, multiply the number of codons in a DNA string by the number of possible codons.

title: Calculate Dimensions for One-hot Encoding
text: Calculate the total number of dimensions for one-hot encoding by multiplying the number of codons by the number of possible codons: $$\frac{3000}{3} 4^3$$.
